clinician.final_diagnosis: Giant malignant melanoma (MM) of the upper limb
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 47-year-old Brazilian woman presented to the ER with a 10×12 cm fungating, cauliflower-like mass on the right arm that had been present for 2 years with progressive growth, accelerating over the preceding 3 months. The mass was friable, ulcerated with necrotic material, and had pustular foul-smelling discharge with intermittent bleeding episodes. She reported associated systemic symptoms including intermittent fever, chills, and weight loss. On examination, she was tachycardic (125 bpm) with pale conjunctiva suggesting anemia. Laboratory studies revealed severe anemia (Hgb 4.2 g/dL), mild leukocytosis (WBC 12.7), elevated reticulocytes (2.34%), and thrombocytosis (Plt 590). Imaging with CT of the right upper extremity showed a large heterogenous soft tissue mass in the superficial mid-upper arm extending into subcutaneous tissues without muscle or bone involvement. The patient underwent surgical resection of the mass (10 cm × 9 cm). The clinical presentation, imaging findings, and surgical management are consistent with giant malignant melanoma of the upper limb.

Superficial location in subcutaneous tissues with overlying skin ulceration and necrosis is more characteristic of melanoma than sarcoma
Persistent 2-year history with progressive growth, imaging showing heterogenous soft tissue mass, and systemic inflammatory response are inconsistent with simple infection

remaining_uncertainties: Histopathologic confirmation of melanoma diagnosis, histologic subtype (superficial spreading vs. nodular vs. acral lentiginous), and staging features (Breslow thickness, ulceration status, mitotic rate, Clark level) were not explicitly documented in available source evidence
Imaging studies for metastatic staging (chest CT, abdominal imaging, brain imaging, or PET-CT) were not documented
Sentinel lymph node biopsy or regional lymph node assessment results were not documented
Complete pathology report from surgical resection specimen was not fully available in source evidence
Treatment decisions beyond surgical resection (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, radiation therapy) were not documented
Clinical course during hospitalization, treatment response, and long-term outcome were not documented
